Check what the chronicler and the kings write against the world

Before an event or a king's declaration is published, the mod checks it against the game: a lord placed in a kingdom he does not belong to, a mercenary called a vassal, a war or an alliance that does not exist, a king claiming another crown's lord as his own. What contradicts the world is thrown away and the reason goes to the log. Reactions to real events may only involve the kingdoms those events touch. Off: everything is published as written.
New campaigns start with every kingdom at peace

Only when a new campaign is created, once, after the game has set up its starting wars: every war between two kingdoms ends. Never on a campaign that already exists and never when loading. Set it before starting the campaign. If a truce length is set below, it counts from that first day. Recommended: off for the game's usual start, on for a calmer first year.
House rule: most kingdoms one kingdom may fight at once (0 = no limit)

An AI king may not declare war if his kingdom, or the kingdom he aims at, is already at war with this many: no piling on. It binds AI kings only. You are never stopped from declaring war yourself, but the rule protects you too: no AI king will declare war on you once you are at the limit. Wars that start by themselves (a rebellion, a new kingdom) are not stopped. Recommended: 2 or 3 to prevent pile-ons; 0 leaves it off.
House rule: days of truce after a peace (0 = none)

After two kingdoms make peace, no AI king of either may declare war on the other until this many days have passed. A year of Calradia is 84 days. It binds AI kings only, in their declarations and when you talk to them: you may break a truce yourself. Recommended: 21 to 84 (84 is one year); 0 turns it off.
House rule: most alliances per kingdom (0 = no limit)

An AI king will not propose or accept an alliance if his kingdom or the other one already has this many. It binds AI kings only: what you propose or accept as ruler is never blocked, but an AI king at his limit will not ally with you. Recommended: 1 or 2; 0 leaves it off.
House rule: most trade agreements per kingdom (0 = no limit)

An AI king will not propose or accept a trade agreement if his kingdom or the other one already has this many. It binds AI kings only, the same way as the limit on alliances. Recommended: 2 to 4; 0 leaves it off.
